_comment: Where provincetown's data wells are. Shape: cartograph/sources.js; the wells themselves live in the state record (cartograph/states/ma.mjs).
_jurisdiction: Provincetown, Massachusetts — Barnstable County. MassGIS TOWN_ID 242 (verified 2026-10-05: the layer's records under TOWN_ID = 242 all read CITY = PROVINCETOWN; 4,955 parcels).
_landUseCodes_why: USE_CODE is Massachusetts' DOR property-class code, read by the state's own vocabulary (states/ma.mjs#readMaDorCode); there is no decode table to fetch.
_cropland_why: USDA's national Cropland Data Layer (cartograph/cdl.mjs): crop rows grow where OSM maps a field and, where it maps none, where the CDL reads crop (Jacob, 2026-10-05). 2024 is the latest year fetched.
_history_why: The MHC inventory (MACRIS points) gives each building its historic name, date, style, maker and designations; joined per building by bake-content.js (geometry, then the parcel's address as a second witness). TOWN_NAME is MHC's spelling (▶ node cartograph/fetch-history.mjs --dry-run prints the count). Fetched by cartograph/fetch-history.mjs --gdb=<MHC_Inventory_GDB.zip>. The National Register nomination (89001148) adds the buildings its narrative names, with dated events cited by page (content/history/nrhp-89001148.json, extracted by hand; meta.method says how). ⭐ ORDER IS PRECEDENCE for a fact both give (year, style, name): the MHC inventory first, as the state's maintained per-building record; a disagreement is reported, and both wells' dated entries are shown.
